subject.title: feat: Let users steer running ACP/sub-agent sessions from Discord (and other chat surfaces)

question: Should ordinary Discord and bound ACP thread messages bypass busy reply-operation/channel admission to reach active-run queue policy by default, and should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89238 be the canonical implementation path?
rationale: The source-level failure is clear, but the permanent fix crosses message-delivery ordering, session-state ownership, and fallback behavior, so maintainer intent is needed before another repair branch should change the routing contract.

options.title: Refresh the admission PR
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89238 as the canonical path, rebase or replace it, and preserve no-visible fallback plus stale-operation recovery semantics before merge.

options.title: Limit ordinary-message steering for now
options.body: Keep ordinary messages queued until a broader ingress design is approved, and document command-only steering as the supported path meanwhile.

options.title: Split Discord ACP follow-up
options.body: Keep https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48003 canonical for general steer admission and track a narrower Discord ACP thread issue only if maintainers want separate ownership.

recommendation.title: Refresh the admission PR
recommendation.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89238 as the canonical path, rebase or replace it, and preserve no-visible fallback plus stale-operation recovery semantics before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and recent history put the central dispatch and Discord queue code under this current-main owner signal, and the remaining choice is about admission/session-state semantics in those files.
